name: Chapter 9 - Opening the economy - Comprehensive MCQ Bank

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three dimensions of international openness distinguished in the chapter?

options.c: The exchange of purely domestic public services between local governments
options.d: Cross-border transactions in goods and services

questions.text: Foreign direct investment is classified in the chapter as:

options.c: a cross-border transaction involving the production factor capital
options.d: a transaction in goods and services only

questions.text: International migration belongs to the dimension of openness involving:

options.c: cross-border transactions on labour as a production factor

questions.text: Under the convention used throughout the open-economy chapters, the nominal exchange rate E is:

options.a: the domestic CPI divided by the foreign CPI
options.b: the price of one unit of domestic currency expressed in units of foreign currency
options.c: the trade-weighted real exchange rate only
options.d: the price of one unit of foreign currency expressed in domestic currency

questions.text: If Europe is the domestic economy and E rises from $1.05 per euro to $1.15 per euro, the euro has:

options.a: experienced a real depreciation regardless of prices

questions.text: With the course convention for E, a depreciation of the domestic currency corresponds to:
The distinction between depreciation and devaluation is that:

options.a: devaluation is always a real exchange-rate change and depreciation is always nominal
options.b: devaluation means E rises under the course convention
options.c: depreciation occurs only under fixed rates
options.d: depreciation refers to a fall in a market-determined exchange rate, whereas devaluation is an official downward change in a fixed central parity

questions.text: A revaluation of the domestic currency under a fixed exchange-rate regime means:

options.a: an official decrease in the central parity E
options.b: a rise in the domestic price level with unchanged parity
options.d: an official increase in the central parity E

questions.text: A crawling peg is best described as:

options.a: a regime in which only the real exchange rate is fixed
options.c: a perfectly floating currency with no intervention
options.d: an intermediate regime in which the central parity is revised periodically

questions.text: A fixed exchange-rate regime generally:

options.a: allows only limited fluctuations around a chosen reference parity/currency
options.b: implies there can never be a devaluation
options.c: fixes the real exchange rate independently of price levels forever
options.d: requires E to change continuously with supply and demand

questions.text: The real exchange rate used in the course is:
Economically, ε = EP/P* measures:

options.a: the number of domestic currency units needed to buy foreign currency
options.b: the domestic nominal interest rate relative to the foreign rate
options.c: the current-account balance in real terms
options.d: the price of a representative domestic basket in units of the foreign basket

Holding E and P* fixed, higher domestic prices P cause:
Holding E and P fixed, higher foreign prices P* cause:

options.a: more expensive relative to foreign goods, implying a loss of price competitiveness
options.b: unaffected because ε is purely nominal

If ε=0.926 in the previous example, the domestic basket is approximately:

options.a: 92.6% more expensive than the foreign basket

questions.text: Why are effective exchange rates constructed?

options.a: A country trades with many partners, so bilateral exchange rates are aggregated using trade weights.
options.b: Because effective exchange rates eliminate the need for price data
options.c: Because only one foreign currency exists in the model
options.d: Because bilateral exchange rates cannot be observed

questions.text: In the nominal effective exchange rate (NEER), bilateral nominal exchange-rate indices are weighted primarily by:

options.a: the relative importance of each trading partner

questions.text: A rise in the real effective exchange rate (REER), using the course convention, indicates:

options.a: an overall real appreciation and deterioration in price competitiveness
options.b: an overall real depreciation and improvement in competitiveness
options.c: a lower domestic price level necessarily

questions.text: The difference between NEER and REER is that REER additionally adjusts for:

options.c: relative domestic and foreign price levels

questions.text: The balance of payments records:

options.a: economic transactions between domestic and foreign economic agents

questions.text: Which item belongs to the current account?

options.a: Changes in central-bank domestic government bonds only
options.c: Purchases and sales of financial assets only
options.d: Purchases and sales of non-produced non-financial assets only

questions.text: The current account groups:

options.c: trade in goods/services, primary income, and secondary income

questions.text: Remittances and foreign aid are classified mainly as:
Wages earned abroad by a domestic resident or dividends received from a foreign firm are examples of:
Transactions in non-produced, non-financial assets such as certain property titles are recorded in:
The financial account mainly records:

options.d: transactions in financial assets and liabilities between domestic and foreign agents

questions.text: GDI is defined as:

options.a: total primary income received by fiscal residents wherever created
options.d: total primary income created on the economy’s territory over a period

questions.text: GNI is defined as:

options.a: total primary income received by fiscal residents/domestic agents over a period
options.c: total primary income created only inside the territory

questions.text: Net income from abroad (NIA) is:
A positive NIA means, on net:

options.b: foreign residents receive more domestic primary income than domestic residents receive abroad
options.c: domestic residents receive more primary income from abroad than foreign residents receive from domestic production
options.d: the trade balance must be positive

questions.text: At the individual level, disposable income after transfers is expressed as:
Gross National Disposable Income (NDI) can be written as:
Net transfers from abroad (NTA) correspond to:

options.a: the net balance of primary factor income
options.c: the net balance of secondary income received from and paid to the rest of the world

questions.text: The chapter warns that macroeconomic NDI is NOT the same concept as:

options.d: Y−T, the disposable-income variable used in the goods-market model

National saving S_N is defined as:
The economy’s funding capacity FC is:

options.b: S_N − I = NDI − C − G − I

questions.text: If FC>0, then:

options.a: the trade balance must be in deficit
options.b: the economy must borrow from abroad
options.d: national saving is more than sufficient to finance domestic investment

questions.text: In a closed economy, funding capacity is necessarily:

options.b: zero, because national saving equals domestic investment

questions.text: The current account is:
The fundamental identity developed in the chapter is:

options.d: CA = FC = NDI − C − G − I

questions.text: A current-account deficit and a trade deficit are:

options.a: synonymous only under floating exchange rates
options.b: not synonymous, because CA also includes NIA and NTA
options.c: unrelated because NX is never in CA

questions.text: A country can have a trade deficit but a current-account surplus if:

options.d: sufficiently positive NIA and/or NTA more than offset negative NX

questions.text: A current-account surplus implies, in terms of saving and investment:
A current-account surplus means the country, on net:

options.a: must have financial liabilities exceeding foreign assets
options.c: exports part of its saving by acquiring foreign assets

questions.text: With the sign convention described in the chapter, a CA surplus is mirrored in the financial account by:

options.c: assets held abroad by domestic residents exceeding liabilities held domestically by foreigners
options.d: assets and liabilities both being zero

questions.text: A current-account deficit indicates that the country:

options.a: imports saving from abroad because domestic funding capacity is insufficient

options.a: Because the domestic interest rate is unknown

questions.text: The exact uncovered interest parity condition is:
The approximate UIR used in the course is:
The UIR is an equilibrium arbitrage condition stating that:

options.a: risk-neutral investors must expect equal returns on comparable domestic and foreign assets
options.c: domestic and foreign nominal interest rates must always be identical
options.d: current and expected exchange rates must always be identical

options.b: equal risk premia across the two assets and no transaction costs
options.c: different risk premia by construction and high transaction costs

questions.text: If domestic investors expect their currency to appreciate, the UIR allows the domestic interest rate to be:

options.b: lower than the foreign interest rate while expected returns remain equal
options.c: identical to the foreign rate in all regimes
options.d: higher than the foreign rate necessarily
